page.layout: One page of text: running head at top centre; italic verse block in the main column; below a rule, a heading block "IN QVINQVE CONSTANTISSIMOS..." with a large initial M opening the elegy verse; signature-like line "Lugduni" at lower right.

main_text.l: Sic propero Vita certus melioris ad astra,
Nec me spes adeo fallere certa potest, Vos mihi, vos lacrymas soli
expressistis amici, Et (fateor) iuestri me superauit amor.
Nec tamen inuitus terras Vitamque relinquo,
Sic patent caeli limina celsa mihi:
Sed, fateor, quoties mentem subiistis amici,
Me quiddam humana conditione pati: Forsan &
hoc, Macrine, legens miserabile carmen
Et quicunque tibi iunctus amicus erit,
Humana memores fortis tergetis ocellos, Et quas
non merui mi dabitis lacrymas. At tibi, quisquis eris,
miseri qui cruda poetae Censueris fletu funera digna tuo,
Hac postrema, precor, sit flendi causa, fluatque Lenis infenso
Vitaque morsque gradu. Quod superest, opto, Beza quos inuidet annos,
Annis adiungat Parca, Macrine, tuis: Vt
nisi post longas charam, Macrine, Gelonin,
Cumque illa Bezam me comitere, moras.
IN QVINQVE CONSTAN-
TISSIMOS Christi Martyres, Lugduni cre-
matos, x v i. Cal. Iunij, Anno Domini
cIo Io LIII. Elegia IV.
Mira loquar, (linguis iuuenesque senesque
fauete)
Digna canam à sera posteritate legi.
Lugduni

page.notes: The scan is slightly cropped at the right edge; several verse lines are faint and some words are doubtful, including the long-s and italic ligature forms, which were read as best possible. The drop-cap M is rendered as a plain letter. The "Lugduni" line at the foot is set at lower right.
